headline: India women refuse Asia Cup trophy from Naqvi after beating Sri Lanka
summary: The Harmanpreet Kaur-led side declined to accept the trophy from ACC president Mohsin Naqvi, echoing a similar stand taken by the men's team last year.
details: India secured their eighth Women's Asia Cup title by defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final in Dubai. However, the victory ended in controversy during the post-match presentation ceremony.

The Indian team refused to receive the trophy or their tournament medals from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president Mohsin Naqvi, who is also the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board and Pakistan's interior minister.

The ceremony was delayed by nearly 50 minutes. While Sri Lanka's players and coaching staff received their runners-up medals and cheque from Naqvi, the Indian side abruptly ended their involvement in the ceremony.
Instead of the official presentation, the Indian team held its own brief medal ceremony. Fielding coach Munish Bali and BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia presented awards to the players.

The decision follows strained cricketing relations between India and Pakistan due to heightened cross-border tensions in May 2025. Indian teams have since avoided handshakes with Pakistani officials and players.
Head coach Amol Muzumdar stated that the team fully supports the BCCI's position, asserting that being champions is enough and the tournament is officially over for them.
caption:
India wins the Asia Cup, but refuses the trophy. Why did the champions decline the award from Mohsin Naqvi?

India secured their eighth Women's Asia Cup title by defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final in Dubai. However, the victory ended in controversy during the post-match presentation ceremony.

The Indian team refused to receive the trophy or their tournament medals from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president Mohsin Naqvi, who is also the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board and Pakistan's interior minister.

The ceremony was delayed by nearly 50 minutes. While Sri Lanka's players and coaching staff received their runners-up medals and cheque from Naqvi, the Indian side abruptly ended their involvement in the ceremony.

Instead of the official presentation, the Indian team held its own brief medal ceremony. Fielding coach Munish Bali and BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia presented awards to the players.

The decision follows strained cricketing relations between India and Pakistan due to heightened cross-border tensions in May 2025. Indian teams have since avoided handshakes with Pakistani officials and players.

Head coach Amol Muzumdar stated that the team fully supports the BCCI's position, asserting that being champions is enough and the tournament is officially over for them.

headline: Drug dealers snatch handcuffed accused from police in Tongi
summary: Attackers hurled stones at a police team during an anti-drug operation, injuring a constable and freeing a warrant-listed accused.
details: Drug dealers allegedly snatched a warrant-listed accused, named Rahul, from police custody while he was in handcuffs at Tongi Railway Station in Gazipur last night.
The incident occurred around 11:00 PM yesterday during an anti-drug operation in the Keranir Tek slum area, where police had arrested Rahul following a tip-off.
While police were transporting the accused, suspected drug dealers attacked the team by hurling stones from the railway tracks, causing chaos and injuring Constable Masud.
Taking advantage of the the attack, the attackers allegedly snatched Rahul from the police. The injured constable received first aid at a hospital.
Additional police forces rushed to the station and cordoned off the area, later recovering the abandoned handcuffs at the scene.
Tongi East Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Maksudul Alam confirmed that Rahul remains at large and operations to recapture him are currently underway.
caption:
Handcuffed and under arrest, but snatched away. Drug dealers allegedly attacked police with stones to free a suspect in Tongi.

Drug dealers allegedly snatched a warrant-listed accused, named Rahul, from police custody while he was in handcuffs at Tongi Railway Station in Gazipur last night.

The incident occurred around 11:00 PM yesterday during an anti-drug operation in the Keranir Tek slum area, where police had arrested Rahul following a tip-off.

While police were transporting the accused, suspected drug dealers attacked the team by hurling stones from the railway tracks, causing chaos and injuring Constable Masud.

Taking advantage of the the attack, the attackers allegedly snatched Rahul from the police. The injured constable received first aid at a hospital.

Additional police forces rushed to the station and cordoned off the area, later recovering the abandoned handcuffs at the scene.

Tongi East Police Station Officer-in-Charge Md Maksudul Alam confirmed that Rahul remains at large and operations to recapture him are currently underway.
